title: Fix ghost-batch amplification causing long-context tail in mixed hosting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported intermittent spikes in 95/99 latency for short requests while a small number of long-context requests were concurrently running. Investigation shows a cluster of "ghost" batches — short-lived admission windows that amplified queued short requests into oversized batches and triggered KV-cache eviction/hand-off churn. This caused a persistent long-context tail and significant token-level cost increases for affected tenants. This ticket tracks the full production fix: prevention, tests, rollout, and monitoring updates.
incidents: 2026-02-16: Enterprise customer 'AcmeSearch' opened a ticket reporting 95th latency spikes for search autosuggest during peak hours (hosted).
2026-02-17: Dedicated customer 'FintechCo' reported increased error rates and latency for low-latency routes coincident with longer-context batch jobs.
2026-02-18: Private deployment (on-prem) surfaced similar pattern during nightly analytics job; site reliability escalated to on-call.
Aggregate symptom: sudden elevation in short-request latency (10–200ms -> 200–800ms) correlated with increased background long-context throughput.
timeline_updates: 2026-02-18: Triage — on-call reproduced correlation in staging using traffic replay. Observed batches containing placeholders for KV handoffs and zero-duration prefetch stalls.
2026-02-20: Root-cause hypothesis formed: admission hysteresis + prefetch handshake creates ghost admission windows that coalesce short requests into large mixed-length batches.
2026-02-25: Spike patch implemented in staging: tight admission window cap + eviction hysteresis; preliminary improvement of 60% in 95th latency for replay tests.
2026-03-02: Code review opened for scheduler admission rewrite (PR #1428). Added e2e harness and deterministic replay for mixed-length flows.
2026-03-08: Canary deploy started on two Hosted clusters and one Dedicated pool with conservative rollout and enhanced tracing.
2026-03-10: Canary shows reduced KV thrash and no regression for long-context throughput; rolling to more clusters pending sign-off.
reproducible_steps: 1) Replay mixed traffic (short requests with occasional long-context requests) against staging scheduler using loadtool 'batch-replay-v2' from artifacts.
2) Enable admission hysteresis flags and prefetch behavior in config to match production defaults.
3) Observe batch composition via /debug/batcher/trace; confirm ghost batches (batches with >60% placeholder entries) occur within 10s windows.
4) Measure 95/99 latency for short-route endpoints while long-context synthetic jobs run concurrently.
root_cause: Admission hysteresis combined with the prefetch/kv-handshake allowed transient admission windows to open and close rapidly. During those transient windows, the scheduler would accumulate short requests into a 'ghost' batch that held KV resources and caused eviction churn. This was amplified under mixed-hosting conditions because Hosted autoscaling and Dedicated reserved pools had different admission-pressure feedback loops, and Private deployments had different ingress shaping causing timing skews.
fix_description: Primary fix rewrites admission window logic to: (a) introduce a minimum stable window duration for batching when prefetch/kv-handshake is active, (b) cap the number of placeholder-prefetch slots allowed per admission window, and (c) add an eviction hysteresis timer to avoid immediate KV handoff on transient spikes. Secondary mitigations include per-tenant admission fairness scoring and a short-request fast-path bypass under high long-context load.
testing_plan: Unit tests for new admission-window semantics (edge cases: zero-duration windows, overlapping handshakes).
Integration tests with deterministic replay harness covering mixed-length distributions and tenant isolation.
Performance bench: compare token/sec and 95/99 latencies vs baseline at 3 load points (low/med/high) on Hosted and Dedicated sims.
Chaos test: introduce synthetic KV eviction jitter to ensure hysteresis prevents oscillation.
Runbook steps validated in staging and added to on-call playbook.
rollout_plan: Canary 1: 2 Hosted clusters (read-only traffic) — 48h monitoring window.
Canary 2: 1 Dedicated pool + 1 Private customer replica (coordination with SRE & customer) — 72h window.
Measure: 95/99 latency regression <= 2% and token-cost drop for affected tenants.
Gradual ramp to 50% capacity, then full rollout if no regressions.
Fallback: runtime flag to revert admission changes instantly; automated rollback if error rate > 0.5% or latency regressions observed.
monitoring: Add batch-composition metric (percent placeholders per batch) and alert when >15% placeholders for >5m.
Dashboard: mixed-length-scheduler-health with per-tenant breakdowns and KV-eviction-rate overlays.
Tracing: sample high-latency short requests to capture batch membership and KV-handshake timeline.
Post-rollout 7-day observation and customer follow-up calls scheduled.
postmortem_notes: Contributing factors: divergent feedback loops between hosting tiers, insufficient guardrails in prefetch handshake logic, and missing observability for placeholder-heavy batches.
Action items: improve invariant tests for scheduler fairness, add a canary that replays mixed-length traces regularly, update runbook with prioritization for placeholder-heavy alerts.
Customer communications: sent incident summary and mitigation timeline to affected customers on 2026-03-09; offer dedicated office hours for large customers.
acceptance_criteria: No >10% regression in long-context throughput after rollout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private testbeds.
95th latency for short routes returns to baseline within 48h of rollout on canary clusters.
Batch placeholder % reduced to <8% on previously affected tenants during similar load profiles.
All new metrics and alerts live and verified; on-call runbook updated and reviewed.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids touching kernel selection code; the fix is scheduler/admission-layer only.
Coordination required with SRE for Dedicated canaries; Private customers must approve canary windows.
Follow-up ticket planned for per-tenant admission tunables (postmortem action).
